First, summarize situation: At T+4 min, FDIR warning FE-401 due to star tracker invalid each of last three orbits (23 min each). Telemetry shows star tracker solution rate dropped to 0 Hz during outages lasting 23 min each, with sun angle at loss ~45.8°, reacquire ~46.1°, min sun angle 40°. Health counter now 3/5, safe mode at 5 -> reaches safe mode at T+146 min per telemetry note. Peak knowledge error 0.46° > limit 0.02°. Burn OM-0417 scheduled T+58 min requiring attitude knowledge <0.02° (REQ-ADCS-010). Build record shows NCR-004: star tracker baffle anodize thickness below drawing, causing increased stray light near sun exclusion angle; sun exclusion test (REQ-ADCS-021) deferred, not flown; asFlown disposition Use-as-is (minor). Onboard sun exclusion table still 35° spec value, but actual exclusion angle is about 46° (as indicated by outages occurring when sun angle ~45.8°). So the tracker loses lock above ~46°, not 35°.

e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**: The star tracker (TM-ADCS-02) has been invalid for three consecutive orbits, each outage lasting 23 min with sun angle at loss ≈45.8° and reacquire ≈46.1° [TM-ADCS-02]. During these outages the vehicle relies on IMU-only propagation, which drifts at 0.02° / min, yielding a peak attitude knowledge error of 0.46° by the end of each outage—well above the 0.02° limit required for the OM-0417 burn [TM-ADCS-02]. The health counter is presently 3 of 5; each outage increments the counter, and at 5 the tracker will be declared failed and the vehicle will enter safe mode, projected to occur at T+146 min [TM-ADCS-02]. The root cause is increased stray light due to an undersized baffle anodize (NCR-004), which was flown “Use-as-is (minor)” and leaves the onboard sun-exclusion table at the spec value of 35° while the actual exclusion angle is ≈46° [NCR-004].

**Why the build record mattered**: The spec sheet predicts no outages above the 35° exclusion angle (REQ-ADCS-021 unverified) and thus would attribute the losses to a generic fault. NCR-004 shows the anodize thickness is 8 µm versus the 12-18 µm drawing, causing more stray light and moving the functional exclusion angle to ≈46° [NCR-004]. This quantitative shift (≈11° higher) explains why the tracker loses lock when the sun angle is 45.8°-46.1°, matching the observed 23-minute outages each orbit. Without this build evidence, the prognosis would incorrectly predict random tracker faults; with it, we see a deterministic pattern tied to orbit geometry and can mitigate by adjusting the onboard exclusion threshold.

**For the operator**:
*At the next pass (Hartebeesthoek, T+70 min)*
- Approve or reject the ONBOARD_TABLE_UPDATE to raise ST_SUN_EXCLUSION_DEG from 35 to 46 (the table change prevents the health counter from reaching 5 and avoids a false safe mode).
- Verify that the burn retime (OM-0417) is being held: check that the sequencer has delayed the burn from T+58 min to the new start time T+84 min.
- Confirm star tracker health counter remains at 3 and that sun angle will exceed 46° at the retime burn (T+84 min) [TM-ADCS-02].
- Log the current outage pattern and note that the next predicted outage (if unchanged) would be T+51 min to T+74 min, which the retime burn avoids [TM-ADCS-02].

*Afterwards*
- After T+84 min: verify OM-0417 executes with attitude knowledge within the 0.02° limit (IMU error should have decayed during tracker validity) and record burn completion.
- After T+146 min: confirm the tracker has not been declared failed and the vehicle remains in normal mode (safe mode not entered) [TM-ADCS-02 health counter].
- Periodically monitor TM-ADCS-02 solution rate and health counter to ensure no further unexpected outages occur.
